newsitem.title: USA: Honeywell wins ruling on circuit boards.
newsitem.headline: Honeywell wins ruling on circuit boards.

text.p: Honeywell Inc said the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit affirmed a lower court's ruling in favor of Honeywell in a lawsuit involving repair services for Honeywell-brand circuit boards.
At issue was a claim by PSI Repair Services Inc, based in Livonia, Mich., that Honeywell's policy on replacement of failed circuit boards violated antitrust laws, Honeywell said.
Honeywell will not sell component parts for its circuit boards to customers or third parties, it said.
PSI asserted the policy prevented it from competing against Honeywell in repair services, Honeywell said.

The court found that "no violation has occurred because Honeywell's policy for replacement of failed circuit boards was consistent and generally known. The court also decided that Honeywell's pricing structure and service policies were well-known and clear," the company said.
PSI Repair Services could not be reached for comment.
